items.title: Connect coding agents to Fabric notebooks with FNTK (Preview)
items.excerpt: The Fabric Notebook Toolkit (Preview) helps developers shorten the feedback loop between writing code and validating it with live notebook results. It connects coding agents to Microsoft Fabric notebooks through a command-line interface (CLI) that runs in the terminal alongside tools such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Codex. An agent can inspect the current code, run one cell, review its output, make a targeted change, and run it again without resubmitting the entire notebook—much as a human programmer working interactively. Figure: Animated GIF A coding agent uses FNTK from the terminal to interact with a Microsoft Fabric notebook. From code suggestions to notebook execution A coding agent can help write a transformation, but a proposed change is not the same as a working result. When execution happens elsewhere, developers must move code into a notebook, run it, and bring the results or errors back to the agent. FNTK connects those steps so the agent can work with a running Fabric notebook and its execution results instead of relying only on code shared in the conversation. items.title: Simplify Teradata migrations with Fabric Migration Assistant (Preview)
items.excerpt: Migrating an enterprise Teradata estate to Microsoft Fabric can require extensive manual work across database objects, SQL and BTEQ code, dependencies, and operational processes. Fabric Migration Assistant helps reduce that effort so teams can focus their review on the objects and workflows that need attention. Fabric Migration Assistant for Data Warehouse now supports Teradata sources in preview. It converts eligible Teradata metadata and code to Fabric-compatible T-SQL, deploys eligible destination definitions, and flags scripts that need review or remediation, reducing the manual effort required to prepare a migration. You can choose which objects to migrate, review the translated code, and focus remediation on exceptions instead of manually translating every eligible object. Migration Assistant does not move the associated data; you load data in the following step of the migration flow. Define a migration scope you can validate Reduce migration risk by starting with a representative set of interdependent objects from one workload or business process. items.title: Manage once, reuse everywhere: Introducing variable library support for Eventstream (Preview)
items.excerpt: Moving a real-time data pipeline from development to test to production should not mean reconfiguring every source and destination. Yet environment-specific connection details and destination references can make each release a manual, error-prone task. Variable library integration with Eventstream in Microsoft Fabric lets teams reuse the same eventstream definition across environments, with references that resolve to each environment's resources. What's new? Variable library integration with Eventstream is available in preview. For supported source connections and destination items, you can use variable library references instead of direct values. These references are preserved through Git integration and deployment pipelines, helping teams reuse an eventstream definition across workspaces with environment-specific configuration. How variable library integration works Variable library is an item type in Microsoft Fabric that provides a centralized way to define and manage configuration values at the workspace level. items.title: Bringing Rust-native Spark compatibility to Microsoft OneLake with Sail and LakeSail
items.excerpt: Coauthor: Shehab Amin Microsoft OneLake gives every Microsoft Fabric tenant a single, unified data lake built on open formats. One copy of data, many engines: that is the promise, and it is what makes OneLake such a strong foundation for analytics and AI alike. This post looks at how Sail , the open-source distributed compute framework, and LakeSail Cloud , the managed platform for running Sail in production, connect natively to OneLake, and what that unlocks for teams running Spark and Python workloads on Fabric. Sail is a drop-in replacement for Apache Spark, rebuilt from the ground up in Rust, with Rust-native support for Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg out of the box. That makes it a natural fit for OneLake, where lakehouse tables are stored in exactly these open formats. Point Sail at a Fabric lakehouse and it reads and writes the same tables the rest of Fabric uses, with no data copies, no extra connectors to install, and no changes to existing Spark code. One engine for data and AI Sail implements the Spark Connect protocol, the gRPC interface that decouples Spark clients from the engine that executes their plans. items.title: T-SQL language enhancements in Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse (Preview)
items.excerpt: Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse is expanding its T-SQL capabilities with four language enhancements in preview. GROUP BY ALL, ORDER BY ALL, the QUALIFY clause, and the FROM ... SELECT query format help SQL developers and data professionals reduce repetitive code, simplify query maintenance, and make analytical logic easier to understand. Figure: A T-SQL query uses GROUP BY ALL and ORDER BY ALL in Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse. What’s new Four T-SQL language enhancements are available in preview: GROUP BY ALL — automatically groups by every non-aggregate expression in the SELECT list, reducing duplication between SELECT and GROUP BY clauses. ORDER BY ALL — sorts results by each column in the SELECT list, using the same column order, so developers do not need to repeat every sort expression. QUALIFY — filters rows after window functions are evaluated, so common ranking and top-N patterns no longer require an additional subquery or common table expression. FROM ... SELECT — provides an alternative query format that begins with the data source and defines the selected columns later, allowing developers to write complex queries in a source-first sequence. items.title: Strengthening data security with workspace-level private connectivity for custom endpoints for Eventstream (Preview)
items.excerpt: Organizations that operate sensitive applications often keep them in networks with no route to the public internet. Applications in restricted networks need real-time analytics without a route to the public internet. Eventstream now supports workspace-level private links for custom endpoint sources (Preview), so those applications can send events to Microsoft Fabric over a private connection. Teams can bring sensitive operational data into real-time analytics without opening a public internet path for ingestion. The change is especially useful for in-house applications, services, and gateways that do not have a managed Eventstream connector. They can publish directly to a custom endpoint source through the workspace’s private connection, bringing these workloads into the same private networking model as supported connector-based sources. What is workspace-level private connectivity? Private Link is a network security feature of the Fabric platform that provides a private connection between a virtual network and Fabric. items.title: More ways to use scalar UDFs in Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse (Preview)
items.excerpt: Scalar user-defined functions (UDFs) let data teams define a business rule once and reuse it across workloads in both Warehouse and the SQL analytics endpoint in Microsoft Fabric. This helps teams maintain consistent logic without duplicating it across queries. Some business rules require more than a single expression. They use procedural logic such as conditional branches, multiple RETURN statements, or WHILE loops. Expression Block inlining compiles and executes this logic in a distributed manner, helping reusable functions scale across analytical workloads. Building on that foundation, this update brings several improvements: More natural loop control and broader query-shape support. Automatic adoption of newly supported capabilities by existing functions, without recreating or altering them. Inlineability validation for new or changed functions, with diagnostics that explain any gaps and an explicit WITH INLINE = AUTO override when a non-inlineable function is acceptable. Express loop intent with BREAK and CONTINUE Loops often need to skip the rest of the current iteration or stop processing entirely. items.excerpt: The October 2026 release of the on-premises data gateway (version 3000.338) continues our commitment to secure, reliable and accessible connectivity between on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric services. This release focuses on accessibility, configuration reliability, and troubleshooting. It makes the installer and configurator more inclusive, keeps your Power Query settings intact during connection tests, and makes service-start failures easier to diagnose. It also brings compatibility updates for the October 2026 release of Power BI Desktop, so queries run the same way in Power BI Desktop and in cloud refreshes. items.title: Govern your Microsoft Fabric data estate from one place with the OneLake catalog and Govern Skills (Generally Available)
items.excerpt: The Govern experience in the OneLake catalog is now generally available, providing centralized governance capabilities for tenants, domains, capacities, workspaces, tags, and policies in Microsoft Fabric. Govern Skills are also now available in the Skills for Fabric collection, giving AI agents the knowledge they need to help admins and data owners audit, investigate, and remediate governance issues at scale. Both were announced at FabCon Europe 2026. Together, they help you monitor, manage, and act on your data estate from one place, whether you work in the Fabric portal or with an AI agent. Why it matters As AI makes it easier for more people to build with data, data estates grow in size and complexity. More workspaces, items, and access requests create more decisions about ownership, organization, and protection. Centralized, proactive governance helps admins support new projects without turning every decision into a manual review or losing visibility into how data is used. Governance can't rely on periodic, manual audits anymore. It needs to be proactive, centralized, and able to scale with the estate. items.title: Announcing workspace monitoring integration for Fabric Data Warehouse (Preview)
items.excerpt: With Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse integration with workspace monitoring (Preview), you can analyze completed warehouse query activity across an entire workspace from the monitoring Eventhouse and KQL database, helping you find failed or slow queries and quickly identify the warehouse that needs attention. See warehouse activity across your workspace Monitoring multiple warehouses is difficult when query activity is spread across separate tools and experiences. Workspace monitoring brings completed warehouse execution events into the WarehouseExecutions table, where administrators and operators can review activity across the workspace from a single monitoring database. The integration supports warehouses, SQL analytics endpoints, and warehouse snapshots. It captures completed, user-initiated queries that use distributed execution and records details such as duration, status, result codes, and CPU time. With this information in one place, you can spot failures or performance issues and focus your investigation on the affected warehouse and query. items.title: Data Visualization in the Agentic Era
items.excerpt: Data visualizations help people identify patterns, trends, and outliers in their data. However, creating a useful visual requires several decisions: which chart and data to use, how to map the data to visual properties such as color and position, and how the finished visual should look. AI-assisted development can reduce that complexity by letting developers describe the intended result in natural language while reusable visualization components handle common design and interaction requirements. Deciding what visualization to create is one problem, while deciding how to create it is another. Power BI offers a convenient way to create reports and visualizations, but authors work within the chart types and formatting options that the product provides. AI coding agents another approach: developers can describe a visualization in natural language and optionally provide example images. Developers no longer have to start with a custom visual implementation or a visualization or graphics specification. Hello!
